findings.message: A failure is caught and cannot be reported. The failure is caught and nothing is returned, so callers get the same value whether the work failed or succeeded. The work is silently lost.

presentations.more: This catches the failure and carries on, and it returns nothing — so a caller has no way to find out. "It failed and I dropped it" and "it worked" arrive at every caller as the same value, however carefully that caller is written, and the work is simply lost. Logging it does not fix this: the log is not where the caller is. Give this method an answer the caller can act on, or let the failure out to whoever awaits it — rethrowing into a call nobody awaits is an unhandled rejection, not a report.

presentations.more: This handler catches the platform's cancellation signal — by its own type or through a supertype — and carries on, so a request to stop becomes an instruction to keep going: the cancelled work runs to the end, whoever cancelled it waits for a completion that no longer means anything, and nothing further up can see that a stop was asked for. Let the cancellation out (rethrow it, or catch a narrower type), or on the JVM restore the interrupt with `Thread.currentThread().interrupt()` before carrying on.
